observation: A three-agent code census before the interview (server, agent side, UI) found what the plan did not know: merge/split/conflicts/promote had no UI, conflicts were never resolved, the edit log had no reader, the sweeps were bound but never called, agents had no tool to read a document. Every founder ruling in the interview was taken against those facts, and the plan was written in one sitting.
evidence: facts.md; plan.md 'What was decided along the way'

observation: Two architecture critiques before any code each returned BLOCKED and each found a class of bug the builders would have shipped: a stored plugin-kind string renamed in the database but not in code; an upsert-by-id that could create over an invisible id; three missed callers of the old package; blocks too big to be worker chunks. The author then dry-ran every block boundary and found seven more ordering breaks.

Cutting the build into ~50 blocks with owned paths, one red test, one verify command and one commit, and running disjoint ones in parallel, meant no worker ran out of budget in 40+ dispatches. Deletions first shrank every later block. The rename wave as one package per worker with a shared exclude list stayed mechanical.
evidence: git log origin/main..HEAD (215 commits); scratchpad preamble.md and rename-brief.md

observation: Files with more than one owner in a phase (app.ts, compose.ts, index.ts barrels) were clobbered or swept into the wrong commit three times when workers ran in parallel. Nothing was lost, but each cost a re-pull and once a git checkout that briefly reverted another worker's WIP.
evidence: worker reports for B11, B12, B19; commit a7b6da1e1 carried a stray import line

observation: The seam test found a hang the package tests could not: edit_document called an injected runner from inside its own transaction and PGlite's single connection never returned. The package test's stand-in for that runner never touched the database. Fix: the test now uses a real lookup and a short timeout so the hang would reproduce.

Five independent reviews (two code, one re-review, one final on the tail, one re-review of the last wave) each FAILED first. Blockers were real: ancestors returned unfiltered (path leaked a sibling team's body); any client could attach a document to an agent or a routine; an artifact search by parent kind alone listed every team's output; item ids in comments; fifteen doc pages left false. Every one was fixed red-first and re-reviewed.

Driving the packaged app found three pre-existing demo/app defects that no test or review saw: the demo founder was on no team (team documents invisible), /auth/me never sent the team (nobody could choose Team scope), and the demo assistant's only session slot was held by a seeded placeholder session (it could never answer). All three were fixed in the seed or the route.

The as-derivation treated a person's private tree document as a memory, so the scope dialog's 'share with team' silently did nothing (server forced the scope back, bumped the version, wrote an empty change row). The plan's words ('a memory is for oneself') did not say whether a private document in the tree is a memory; the app's own list already had a Private pill and a separate Memories filter. Ruled during the walk: a memory is a private note with no parent and an ordinary slot; a private tree document is a document. Founder to confirm at the gate.

Three pure invariants were keyed on the literal input word (as, slot) and missed edits of an existing row: a memory given a team scope was silently forced, an existing artifact could be made private. The architecture's combined cases were written per input, not per 'existing row + partial edit'. Fixed by keying on the effective value (input else the row's derived one); I5/I6 deliberately stay literal so graduation works.

Founder answers at the amendment gate reversed two architecture defaults: the scope cascade stays (built honestly, one change row per child) instead of a refusal, and usage counts are kept and made real (with the plugin's decay routine archiving unused documents) instead of dropped with the side table. The first estimate of −3,300 net production lines became about −3,100 once those were built; the whole-diff net is small because the rename touches 640 files neutrally.

Stale gitignored dist/*.d.ts and tsbuildinfo of referenced packages invented or hid type errors for at least six workers; each lost time before rebuilding declarations. The rule went into the shared preamble mid-run. A full tsc -b also scatters .js/.d.ts into tools/governance/src that the governance lint then flags.
evidence: worker reports B0b, B0c, B1, B2c, B2d, B3

observation: One interview (six rulings), one architecture (2,200 lines) with two critiques and three amendments, ~50 build chunks plus ~12 fix/gate chunks, 5 independent reviews (all FAIL first) with 5 fix waves, 3 full gate runs, one full e2e comparison against main, one real-harness lane on four harnesses, four packaged desktop builds and two manual walks. Rework: roughly a third of the chunks were review fixes, gate fixes or re-points of tests that mocked deleted routes. Result: 215 commits, production code +8,065 / −11,173, whole diff about +30k / −32k.
evidence: git log; scratchpad gate logs; task notifications
